text: The banais ríghe is the Irish feast of inauguration. It marked the sacred marriage of the king and the land. In the rite the goddess of Sovereignty wed her chosen king. The bond tied his fortune to the land. One old account says the king mated with a white mare. The mare was then killed and boiled into a broth. The king drank the broth. This feast joins inauguration to the horse sacrifice.
